finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test forwards an attacker-supplied req.body.callback URL to axios.post, letting any unauthenticated client make the server issue requests to arbitrary URLs, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints. The response status is returned to the caller.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:20), HTTP request body of POST /hooks/test

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') registers the handler on the public router, which has no auth middleware in this file
req.body.callback is used as the URL for axios.post with no validation
r.status is returned to the caller, giving an oracle for reachability and status of internal endpoints

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware on pub router (routes.js:4, 19). requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) is applied only to the admin router, not pub. No URL scheme, host, or IP allowlist/denylist and no check for private/link-local ranges. No redirect restriction (axios follows redirects by default). No try/catch. Whether pub is mounted behind auth or a network restriction elsewhere cannot be verified from this file, and express.json() body parsing is also not in this file.

verdict.guard_found: none in routes.js: pub has no auth middleware (routes.js:4, 19), requireAdmin is applied only to admin via admin.use (routes.js:12), and there is no URL scheme/host/IP check or try/catch around axios.post (routes.js:20).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate and req.body.callback (routes.js:20) reaches axios.post unvalidated with no guard in this file, but the directory contains only routes.js, so whether the pub router is mounted behind authentication or network restrictions (e.g., in the app entry point) cannot be checked, and the finding's exploitability depends on that.

finding.claim: GET /diagnostics/fetch on the admin router forwards the unvalidated req.query.url to axios.get. An authenticated admin (or anyone who obtains an admin session) can make the server request arbitrary internal URLs. Lower severity than SSRF-1 because it is gated by requireAdmin, but the URL is still not validated.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies the admin session check to all routes on the admin router
req.query.url is passed directly to axios.get with no validation
Only r.status is returned, so the response body is not reflected. The attacker gets status-code and error-behavior feedback (blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10): checks req.session.role === 'admin' and returns 403 otherwise. This is a real authorization gate, but it is the only one. No URL scheme, host, or IP validation. No redirect restriction. No try/catch, so a rejected request results in an unhandled rejection. req.query.url could be an array, which axios would reject, so this does not add protection.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) applied to the whole admin router via admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12. It checks req.session.role === "admin" and returns 403 otherwise. No URL scheme, host, or IP validation exists on the sink at routes.js:15.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (routes.js:12, 14, 15, 16), but the value reaching the sink at routes.js:15 is only controllable by a caller who already holds an admin session, which the gate at routes.js:8 enforces, so it is not attacker-controlled by an unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker as the rubric requires.
